checks.comparison: Assumption 1 (line 332) requires each f_i twice continuously differentiable; the clause states exactly C^2 for every f_i : R^p -> R. Lean: Assumption1 conjunct ContDiff R 2 (f i) for every i, in spec.admissible.

Line 332: constants 0 < m <= M < infinity with mI <= grad^2 f_i(x) <= MI for all x in R^p. The clause encodes the Loewner bounds as quadratic-form bounds for all v, which is the meaning of the order on symmetric matrices (line 111 defines it for symmetric matrices; Hessians of C^2 functions are symmetric). m, M are outer parameters as required because the step-size conditions use them. Lean: forall x v, m*||v||^2 <= <fderiv R (gradient (f i)) x v, v> <= M*||v||^2, with the same Hessian object the oracle returns; 0 < m and m <= M are in spec.valid.

Assumption 2 (line 372): grad^2 f_i are L-Lipschitz; matrix norm is the Euclidean (spectral = operator) norm by the notation of line 108. Clause: ||grad^2 f_i(x) - grad^2 f_i(y)|| <= L||x - y|| in operator norm for all i, x, y. Lean: Assumption2: forall i x y, ||fderiv R (gradient (f i)) x - fderiv R (gradient (f i)) y|| <= L * ||x - y|| (operator norm of continuous linear maps); 0 <= L in spec.valid.
Line 338 and line 393: a = M + 2(1 - w_min)/lambda. Clause identical. Lean: a p = p.M + 2 * (1 - wmin p.toPublic) / p.lam (checked by rfl).

Line 338: w_min = min_i w_ii. Clause identical; needs n >= 1, recorded in NET/agents. Lean: wmin q = iInf i, W i i; for 0 < n (Network) this is attained, i.e. equals min_i w_ii (checked in Lean: exists i, wmin q = W i i, via exists_eq_ciInf_of_finite).

Eq. (P2), line 124: F(x) = h(x) + (1/(2 lambda)) x^T(I - Z)x. Clause identical. Lean: penalty q f x = sum_i f i (x i) + 1/(2 lam) * <x, x - mix x>, with the PiLp 2 inner product sum_i <x^i, y^i>; equals h(x) + x^T(I - Z)x/(2 lambda).

Line 126: Z = W (x) I in R^{np x np}. The clause adds the componentwise reading (Zx)^i = sum_j w_ij x^j, a direct expansion of the Kronecker product, consistent with (traditionl method) line 132. Lean: Z is represented by mix q x = (sum_{j in N_i u {i}} W i j • x j)_i; under Network's sparsity clause W i j = 0 for j not in N_i u {i}, so mix x = (W (x) I)x. Since spec.valid contains Network, every use of penalty in the spec is with this identification; the equality is a planned Proofs lemma (mix_apply_eq_sum).

Line 129: grad F(x_k) = grad h(x_k) + (1/lambda)(I - Z)x_k, grad h = (grad f_1(x^1),...,grad f_n(x^n)). Clause identical; it is the true gradient since I - Z is symmetric (W symmetric). Lean: penaltyGradient = toLp (fun i => gradient (f i) (x i) + (1/lam) • (x i - mix x i)) = grad h(x) + (I - Z)x/lambda.
Line 126: h(x) = sum_i f_i(x^i). Clause identical. Lean: the first summand of penalty, sum_i f i (x i).

Line 204: grad^2 h(x) is block diagonal with blocks grad^2 f_i(x^i); line 249 and Lemma 5's proof (line 399) use grad^2 F = grad^2 h + (1/lambda)(I - Z). Clause matches. Lean: penaltyHessian x v = toLp (fun i => fderiv R (gradient (f i)) (x i) (v i) + (1/lam) • (v i - mix v i)) = (blockdiag grad^2 f_i(x^i) + (I - Z)/lambda) v.

Params extends Public with m, M, L : R and k : N; Instance = Fin n -> EuclideanSpace R (Fin dim) -> R (local objectives), Query = Output = Stacked = R^{np}, Reply = LocalReply. valid imposes Network, 0 < lam, 0 < eta, 1 <= K, 0 < m, m <= M, 0 <= L: exactly the accepted parameter domains (M < infinity is automatic for a real).

All spec predicates are evaluated at p.toPublic and the same instance f; Delta = penalty f x0 - penalty f xstar in admissible and successful uses the same xstar quantifier structure as the accepted plan (for every minimiser in admissible; the existential minimiser in successful); a, rate and the step-size predicates use p's m, M, L, eta, K, lam and wmin of p.toPublic.

Polarity: valid and admissible are hypotheses of Convergence, successful its conclusion. successful = exists xstar, IsMinOn penalty univ xstar and 0 < rate < 1 and a.e. F(output) - F(xstar) <= (1 - rate)^k Delta. Because all minimisers have the same value and one exists (DMIN), this equals the source's statement for 'the minimum point' x_*; admissible's 'for every minimiser' likewise equals the source's single condition. Checked by Iff.rfl that admissible and allowedAlgorithm elaborate exactly as written.

Every TH2 context hypothesis appears once: NET (Network), TH2/pos (0 < lam, 0 < eta, 1 <= K), (29) (StepSizeLemma5) in valid; A1, A2, TH2/stepT (StepSizeTheorem2 at Delta) in admissible; 0 < m <= M and 0 <= L in valid; TH2/min as IsMinOn. The only non-source hypothesis is oracle correctness (forall k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = localOracle f x), the DEXEC/hyp template hypothesis. Nothing else is assumed.

StepSizeLemma5: eta < 1, eta < 1/a, eta < 2m/(a^2 K^2) = (29). StepSizeTheorem2: eta < m/(a^2K^2) and eta^2 * (a^4 (2a)^{3/2} K^3 L Delta^{1/2}) < 6 m^5 with real exponents (3/2 : R), (1/2 : R) = the accepted corrected, cleared condition. rate = (2m^2 eta - m a^2 eta^2 K^2)/a - a^3 (2a)^{3/2} eta^3 K^3 L/(6m^3) * Delta^{1/2}; I checked in Lean that it equals the epsilon formula with sqrt Delta (simp with Real.sqrt_eq_rpow), confirming the parse ((... * L)/(6m^3)) * Delta^{1/2}.

Oracle correctness is required for every call index, query and oracle seed, so execution is seed-independent; successful uses an a.e. statement over the template's product law, which holds pointwise. Faithful to the deterministic source.
